personas.pick: GitHub Copilot Free in VS Code, plus ChatGPT Study Mode or Claude free to explain things
personas.why: Free, works in the most popular editor, and the chatbots teach rather than just answer.

personas.pick: GitHub Copilot Student (free) plus the JetBrains Student Pack
personas.why: Verified students get unlimited completions and 200 AI credits a month free; JetBrains IDEs are free too.
Unlimited completions and a choice of top models for the price of a lunch. Antigravity is a free alternative.

personas.who: Already pay for ChatGPT or Google AI
personas.pick: Use what's included: Codex with ChatGPT Plus (A$30), or Antigravity + Jules with Google AI Pro (A$32.99)
personas.why: No extra cost; try these before adding another subscription.

personas.pick: Claude Pro (for Claude Code) + GitHub Copilot Pro
personas.why: The most common pairing: a strong agent for big changes plus fast autocomplete in your editor.
Everything in one polished editor with models from several companies.
Pro tiers stop you hitting 5-hour limits mid-task; ChatGPT Pro currently has no 5-hour Codex limit.

personas.pick: Codex CLI with a local model (Ollama), or Cline/OpenCode with local models
personas.why: Nothing leaves your computer. Needs a recent computer with 16–32 GB of memory, and local models are less capable.

privacy_tips: Most individual plans can use your code for training by default. Check the setting on day one.
Business and team plans almost always exclude your code from training. Worth it if you code for clients or an employer.
Turning training off doesn't stop your code being sent to the company's servers; only local models do that.
